s1.syndrome_frame: Altered mental status with catatonia and autonomic dysfunction
salient_findings: Disturbed consciousness with Glasgow scale score of 7
Rigidity, negativism, mutism, catalepsy, waxy flexibility, and stupor
Elevated creatine phosphokinase (CPK) and liver enzymes
key_facts: 44-year-old man with a history of schizophrenia
Under antipsychotic treatment (risperidone) with antiparkinsonian drug (Biperiden)
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score of 25/69
Unremarkable chest X-ray and cerebral CT
Round lesion in the splenium of the corpus callosum on brain MRI with restricted diffusion

shortlist.label: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is under antipsychotic treatment and presents with fever, rigidity, and elevated CPK

shortlist.label: Malignant Catatonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a high Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score and presents with catatonic symptoms

shortlist.label: Serotonin Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is under antipsychotic treatment which can cause serotonin syndrome, and presents with autonomic dysfunction

shortlist.label: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has altered mental status and a round lesion in the splenium of the corpus callosum on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Catatonic Schizophrenia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of schizophrenia and presents with catatonic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including rigidity, negativism, mutism, catalepsy, waxy flexibility, and stupor, along with a high Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score of 25/69, are characteristic of catatonia. The presence of fever, tachycardia, elevated CPK, and leucocytosis, in the context of catatonia, suggests a malignant form. The brain MRI findings, although unusual, do not directly contradict this diagnosis, and the complete resolution of the lesion could be related to the treatment of the underlying condition.

rejected.label: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient is on antipsychotic treatment, the primary symptoms and the context suggest catatonia rather than neuroleptic malignant syndrome as the primary issue.

rejected.label: Serotonin Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no clear indication of recent changes in serotonergic medications or other factors that would typically precipitate serotonin syndrome.

rejected.label: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
rejected.why: The presentation and the imaging findings do not strongly support an autoimmune encephalitis, and there's no mention of specific tests for anti-NMDA receptor antibodies.

rejected.label: Catatonic Schizophrenia
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of schizophrenia, the acute presentation with fever, tachycardia, and elevated CPK suggests a more severe and potentially life-threatening condition than catatonic schizophrenia alone.

rejected.label: Serotonin Syndrome
rejected.why: The lack of specific serotonergic medication changes and the presence of catatonic symptoms point away from serotonin syndrome as the primary diagnosis.
